text: Priya's in — if you split the company. A co-founder halves the loneliness. Also the cap table.

right.label: Go solo. All gas, all equity.

text: No co-founder, then. Just you and a Claude subscription. It says it's 'genuinely excited' about your idea. It says that about everything.

right.label: It's fancy autocomplete and we both know it

text: So how does this get paid for, exactly? Your mother is asking for a friend. The friend is her.

right.label: Keep the day job, build at night

text: Headquarters options: your garage, or a coworking space with 'community energy' and a ping-pong tax.
How do we enter the world? I vote loud. I always vote loud.
The garage has reached capacity. Also, technically, it's your mom's, and she wants to park there again.
You and your co-founder disagree on the roadmap. Loudly. In front of everyone. People are wearing headphones that aren't plugged in.
You hit a wall. Your co-founder notices, closes the laptop, and drags you out for the good burritos.
The rift didn't heal. Priya offers a clean split: buy her out, or fix this like adults, in therapy. Founder therapy. It's a thing.
'We don't fund tourists,' Doug says, eyeing your work badge from the day job. 'Founders jump. Tourists visit.'
I audited our spending. We pay for 14 SaaS tools, 3 do the same thing, and the kombucha nobody drinks anymore.
I can halve the cloud bill: reserved instances, and we delete the staging environment named 'staging-final-2'. Nobody knows what it does.
We need extra marketing resources for the product launch.
A billboard on the 101. Every serious startup has one. It's basically free money.
There's a productivity influencer with 2M followers. For $40K he'll call us 'a game changer'.
The brand feels stale. I'm thinking: same product, but the logo is a gradient now.
I'm launching a company podcast. Working title: 'Growth Mindset with Chad'. I need a mic budget.
Our competitor's CEO is having a very public meltdown. I've drafted 17 tweets. Some are art.
Chad posted on LinkedIn about 'founders who don't invest in growth'. Everyone knows who he means.
Signups are flat since Chad left. Turns out the cringe LinkedIn posts... worked?
Chad joined your biggest competitor. His first campaign: 'Time to switch?' It has a billboard.
The codebase is held together with duct tape and one cron job nobody understands. I need a month to refactor.
Everything is down. The cron job woke up. I warned you about this.
The AWS rep called. Your 'blame AWS' post went around their office. Our startup discount is mysteriously gone.
Found a brilliant engineer. She wants market salary. Actual market, not 'startup market'.
She took the FAANG offer. The team saw the salary she posted. They're doing math.
I haven't slept since the demo. I can see the code when I close my eyes. It's mostly red.
I'm resigning. My therapist and my rubber duck both agree.
My condition for staying: four-day week for engineering. Tech Twitter found out and has opinions.
Production is down. The only person who understood the deploy script left. The script's comments are in emoji.
I know a 'rockstar CTO' who's available. Rockstar prices, rockstar equity, rockstar keynote habit.
The intern-CTO ran a 'quick cleanup script' on production. We now have zero users. In the database sense.
Data says users ignore the product and only use the screenshot tool we built in a weekend.
Press loves the pivot story. 'The Screenshot Company' is trending. Our old customers are... confused.

right.label: Keep the old product on life support

text: Internal hackathon? Two days, no meetings, pizza budget. The team needs a win.
We've outgrown the database. Two weeks of migration pain now, or outage roulette forever.
The database fell over. During the investor demo. The spinner is still spinning.
Someone found our API keys on GitHub. In a repo named 'temp-final-FINAL-2'.
A security researcher found the breach we didn't disclose. Their write-up has 40K upvotes and a meme format.
Sales promised a client 'AI-powered blockchain analytics'. What we have is a CSV export.
The team is asking for a kombucha tap. It's $2K a month. I know. I said that too.
Landlord is raising rent 40%. He says it's 'the market'. He says that every year.
Team offsite proposal: two days, cabins, trust falls optional. Quotes attached.
The printer is making a sound I can only describe as 'legal liability'.
Half the team wants full remote. The other half wants the office. Everyone wants you to decide by Friday.
200 intern applications. We can afford to pay one, or take five 'for the exposure'.
A letter from the EU. We are, apparently, 'processing personal data'. The fine has a lot of zeros.
A user emailed: our product saved their bakery. They attached a photo of a thank-you cake.
Mom is calling. She wants to know if you're eating and what a 'runway' is.
Sweetie, I have $10K saved. Take it. Your father agrees, and he never agrees.
At Thanksgiving, Mom asks how her 'investment' is doing. Grandma is listening. Grandma remembers everything.
Mom laminated the article about your company and gave copies to the whole neighborhood.
TechCrunch wants an interview. They asked about our 'AI strategy'. We don't have one.
Users are demanding the AI features from that interview. The ones that don't exist.
TechDisrupt wants $50K for a booth between a juicero revival and a blockchain gym.
You're invited to keynote a conference. It's the same week as the product launch. Of course it is.
A journalist is writing 'The Dark Side of Your Startup'. They want a comment by Thursday.
We're shortlisted for 'Startup of the Year'. Gala tickets are $10K a table. Doug will be there.
Google just launched a clone of our product. It's worse, but it's free and preinstalled.
We're trending. A celebrity used the product on a livestream. This is not a drill.
Payroll clears in three weeks. After that, vibes. We need to cut something.
New Glassdoor review: 'Great snacks, sudden layoffs.' It's the first Google result for our name now.
Half the team has LinkedIn open on a second monitor. They stopped hiding it.
A law firm in Texas claims you infringed their patent on 'displaying information on a screen'. They want $80K.
An enterprise client offers $150K — if you build their custom SSO-SAML-LDAP dashboard by Q3.
A famous advisor offers to 'open doors' for 2% equity. The doors are not specified.
An investor wants in — if you 'put the roadmap on-chain'. He says 'ser' unironically.
Your crypto investor got indicted. His tweets tagging us are Exhibit C.
Doug wants to grab coffee. 'No agenda,' he says, opening a notebook titled 'Agenda'.
First board meeting. Doug wants 'T2D3 with negative churn'. You nod and write down letters.
The board wants a 'grown-up CFO'. The phrase 'adult supervision' was used. About you.
Doug called the other investors. There was a 'vote of confidence'. About you. You weren't invited.
Legal says new hires' options come out of YOUR shares. It was in the paragraph. The one nobody reads.
I like the cut of your jib. $300K for 10%. I also said 'jib' to the last twelve founders.
Seed round: $1M at a $5M post-money. Clean terms. Well. Clean-ish.
Better offer: $1.2M at $5.5M! Standard terms. Don't worry about the option pool paragraph. Nobody reads the option pool paragraph.
Series A: $4M at a $20M post. There will be a board now. The board will have opinions.
Series B: $10M at a $60M post. You now employ someone whose whole job is buying chairs.
Word is you're running on fumes. Bridge round: $200K for 8%. Fumes are expensive.
A competitor offers a $2M acquihire. 'It's a good outcome,' they say. They say it twice.
BigCorp offers $30M cash for the company. All of it. Signed by Friday.
BigCorp came back. $45M this time. The banker says 'final offer' in a tone that means it.
A strategic acquirer offers $8M. 'Your team would love our campus. We have four cafeterias.'

right.label: We have a microwave and a dream

text: The bankers are here. NASDAQ. Ticker symbol picked. You'd ring an actual bell.
A billionaire tweeted 'I should buy this' about your company at 3am. His lawyers confirmed he's serious. Ish.

left.label: Sell for $50M before he sobers up

text: A private equity firm offers $12M. They use the word 'streamline' four times. Your team's faces fall.
A SPAC named after a Greek god wants to take you public. Their last three deals are down 90%. But the god is Zeus.
I found a guy who can get us 50K users overnight. Don't ask how. Seriously, don't ask.
Due diligence found that 40% of your users are named 'user_test_final2' and log in from the same IP.
Super Bowl ad slot. Thirty seconds. We have Series A money now. Think BIG.

right.label: We are not a beer brand

text: The brand account should be unhinged now. All the big brands are unhinged. It's called relatability.
Merch drop: hoodies with the logo. Employees get one free. Everyone else pays $80. For our logo.
We need a TikTok. I've been practicing a dance. It's called 'The Burn Rate'. I will not be stopped.
Proposal: rewrite everything in Rust. It'll take four months and fix problems we don't technically have yet.
The on-call rotation is me, myself, and my other phone. I need at least one more person carrying a pager.

right.label: The app rarely crashes at night

text: Let's open-source the core engine. Free contributors, community love, conference talks.
A cloud giant forked our open-source engine and launched it as a managed service. They sent a fruit basket.

left.label: Change the license, start a war

text: Every competitor added a chatbot. Ours would cost $30K a month in API calls to mostly apologize.
An ex-employee is suing over the 'unlimited vacation' policy. Their lawyer found the Slack message. You know the one.
Someone brought a dog. Productivity is down 30%. Happiness is up immeasurably. The dog's name is Sprint.
HR wants a 'culture deck'. 80 slides about our values. Slide 41 is just the word 'HUSTLE' in flames.
The accountant found an error. We've been paying for 40 seats of software we've never opened. For a year.
A customer is demanding a refund. On the plaza. With a megaphone. Local news is setting up a tripod.
Mom is visiting the office. She brought food for everyone and is asking Doug if he has 'a real job'.
Mom joined LinkedIn. She comments 'So proud!! Call me' on every company post. Investors have noticed.
Doug wants a real-time metrics dashboard in his office. 'Just the north star KPIs.' He lists fourteen.
Doug proposes a 'recapitalization'. The math is confusing on purpose. Your equity is the confusing part.
Doug wants to introduce you to BigCorp's corp dev team. 'Just to build the relationship.' Sure, Doug.
Investor summit on a yacht. Three days of 'networking'. Someone will say 'synergy' at you. Repeatedly.
My feng shui consultant looked at your office photos. The servers face north. This explains everything, allegedly.
We're on the Hacker News front page. Comment #1: 'I built this in a weekend.' Comment #2 is worse.
Finance says we lose money on every free user. Marketing says free users are 'the funnel'. Both have charts.
Churn doubled this month. Exit surveys all say the same thing: 'I forgot what this app does.'
Our biggest competitor just shut down. Their users are flooding in. So are their support tickets.
Someone is mining crypto on our free tier. Their usage graph looks like a hockey stick. The bad kind.
Claude wrote 80% of the codebase. Claude would now like to refactor the codebase. It has prepared a 14-step plan and three apologies.
Production is down. Claude says you're absolutely right to be frustrated, and that the bug is in the file it wrote. In step 9 of 14.
You hit the rate limit at 2am, mid-launch. The message suggests 'taking a break'. From your own product launch.
The codebase no longer fits in context. Claude keeps rediscovering the payments module and calling it 'interesting'.
You left 12 Claude agents running overnight. They shipped nine features, two tests, and one philosophical manifesto about naming variables.

left.label: Ship all of it, read nothing

text: Claude declines to write the competitor-scraping bot. It cited the site's terms of service. Your terms of service.
A competitor rebuilt our entire product as a ChatGPT wrapper. In a weekend. It has more users than us.
Nobody googles anymore. Perplexity answers questions about our product now — confidently, and wrong. It says we're a pet food brand.
Doug asks what our 'AI story' is. You describe the product. He asks again, slower: what is the A. I. story.
OpenAI is down and half the industry is on Twitter pretending they aren't refreshing the status page. Our product still works.
The intern pasted the entire customer database into ChatGPT to 'clean up the formatting'.
Every SaaS we use added an AI assistant nobody asked for and doubled their prices to pay for it.
